newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-NETS, MAVERICKS LOSE AS NEW LINEUPS DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-NETS, MAVERICKS LOSE AS NEW LINEUPS DEBUT.

text.p: The New Jersey Nets and Dallas Mavericks sent their new lineups into battle on Thursday with the same old results -- defeat.
At New Jersey, Tim Hardaway scored 23 of his 35 points in the second half as the Miami Heat extended their winning streak to 11 games with a 92-87 victory over the Nets.
Alonzo Mourning added 16 points and Jamal Mashburn 10 for the Heat, who improved to 24-6 on the road.
Sam Cassell, acquired in Monday's nine-player trade with Dallas, and Kendall Gill each had 17 points for the Nets.
Eric Montross and Chris Gatling, also picked up in the big trade, each had double-doubles. Montross scored 12 points and pulled down 11 rebounds, while Gatling added 13 and 10.
"92-87, that ain't bad," said Nets coach John Calipari of his revamped roster. "For a first game ... I thought it was terrific."
The Nets led 70-69 late in the third quarter, but Hardaway hit a pair of jumpers to ignite a 17-4 Miami run.
In Dallas, Vin Baker had 29 points and 12 rebounds Ray Allen added 17 points as the Milwaukee Bucks survived a late run by the all-new Mavericks for a 101-99 victory.
Michael Finley had a career-high 33 points, including 15 in the third quarter, for the Mavericks, who have no players left from last year's lineup.
Centre Shawn Bradley made his Dallas debut with 10 points, 10 rebounds and six blocks, while fellow former Nets Khalid Reeves contributed eight points and Ed O'Bannon, four.
"Hopefully we'll get the chance to run up and down in practice, get these guys familiar with offensive and defensive sets and come out Saturday and get a victory," Finley said.
In Sacramento, Patrick Ewing scored 24 points and grabbed 11 rebounds as the New York Knicks used their best shooting effort of the season to crush the Kings 109-87.
All five starters scored in double figures for the Knicks, whose winning streak reached seven games to remain two back of the first-place Heat in the Atlantic Division.
Larry Johnson added 22 points and Charles Oakley chipped in with 15 and 12 rebounds as the Knicks shot 59 percent from the field (41-of-69) and held the Kings to just 10 points in the third quarter.
Mitch Richmond led Sacramento with 25 points.

At Indiana, Rik Smits scored 23 points and grabbed a career-high 16 rebounds and Antonio Davis added 14 points and 11 boards as the Pacers beat the Denver Nuggets 92-68 just hours after the teams swapped six players.
The Pacers scored the first nine points and never trailed.
LaPhonso Ellis had 18 points and nine rebounds and Antonio McDyess added 17 and nine for the Nuggets.
None of the six players in the deal played Thursday, but veteran guard Mark Jackson received a big ovation from Indiana fans upon arriving to re-join his former team.
In Houston, Hakeem Olajuwon scored 25 points and Kevin Willis chipped in 20 points and 10 rebounds off the bench as the Rockets beat the Toronto Raptors 107-97.
Charles Barkley added 18 points, including consecutive three-pointers in a key third-quarter run for the Rockets.
Olajuwon, who also grabbed eight rebounds and blocked two shots, made 12-of-17 shots from the field, including scoring his 23,000th career NBA point.
Damon Stoudamire scored 17 points, Popeye Jones added 16 and Doug Christie had 15 for Toronto.
At Utah, Karl Malone had 34 points, 16 rebounds and eight assists to lead the Jazz to a 122-105 win over the hapless Boston Celtics.
Bryon Russell added 18 points and John Stockton had 15 points and 11 assists for the Jazz, who have won seven in a row and raised their home record to 25-2.
The Jazz shot 57 percent (47-for-83) from the field and outrebounded Boston 52-27.
David Wesley and Todd Day each scored 21 points for the Celtics, losers of the first eight games of their nine-game road trip.

In Philadelphia, Allen Iverson had 24 points and 13 assists and Derrick Coleman added 21 points and 20 rebounds as the 76ers snapped a five-game losing streak with a 101-84 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.
Clarence Weatherspoon scored 24 points and grabbed 10 rebounds, while Jerry Stackhouse contributed 17 points for Philadelphia, which won for just sixth time in 37 games.
Darrick Martin scored 12 points and Rodney Rogers and Lorenzen Wright each had 11 for the Clippers.
